rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> two-year split-plot field experiment at CCRI Multan (2009-2010), drip vs furrow in main plots, weed treatments in subplots, three replications, 7 m x 3 m plots. Q2: Results, 'Weed density' section and Table 1 <U+2013> all drip-irrigated treatments showed a significant 19-24% decrease in total weed density at 60 DAS compared with furrow irrigation (I1 77.9 and 87.5 vs I2 102.7 and 108.4 weeds m-2); weed dry matter also lower under drip (69.9/84.7 vs 101.3/114.0 g m-2).
rows.notes: Weed density counts and weed dry weight are the same field-sampling method, so no triangulation. The mechanism (drip confines moisture to the crop root zone, limiting water to weeds) is asserted with a citation to Choudhary et al. 2012, not measured; soil moisture was not reported. Single site, single crop (one cultivar), plot scale. No support factors or limitations stated by the authors. Only LSD values and letter groupings are given in Table 1; no SD/SE/CI for the weed-density result, and the 19-24% figure is a spread across years rather than a dispersion measure.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> own two-year field experiment in cotton at Multan, Pakistan, with drip and furrow irrigation as main-plot treatments. Q2: Results 'Weed density' section and Table 1 <U+2013> drip irrigation reduced weed density (19-24%) and weed dry matter at 60 DAS relative to furrow irrigation in both years; Discussion restates that drip irrigation significantly suppressed weed population and dry matter.
rows.notes: Same evidence base as the first row. Single method (field weed sampling), one site and crop, plot scale, mechanism asserted via citation rather than measured, no stated conditions or limitations, and only LSD/letter groupings reported rather than a dispersion measure.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract, methods, results tables 1-4, discussion, references). The study is a single-site, two-year split-plot field trial in cotton comparing drip and furrow irrigation combined with herbicide/manual weed control; the drip-vs-furrow weed effect is a direct own result but is reported only with LSD and significance letters.
